# Customs Clearance Workflow Update

Date: 2024-03-23  
Attendees: Oriel Fennvane, Odalys Naskdale, Nadezhda Ibbton  

## Agenda  
- Review current customs clearance documentation verification process  
- Analyze risk assessment model accuracy and false positive rates  
- Propose enhancements to improve clearance throughput and reduce delays  

## Discussion  
Oriel presented current verification metrics: average processing time per container is 18 minutes, with a 4.6% documentation rejection rate due to incomplete or inconsistent paperwork. Odalys highlighted that the risk assessment model flags 12% of shipments as high risk, but only 2.8% of those actually require additional inspection, indicating a 76% false positive rate. Nadezhda suggested that incorporating real-time crane telemetry data could cross-validate container contents, potentially reducing manual inspection workload. The team debated prioritizing automation of document verification vs. refining risk scoring thresholds.  

## Decisions  
- Pilot integration of crane telemetry into risk assessment starting April 1, targeting a 25% reduction in false positives  
- Update document submission portal to include mandatory real-time validation checks by May 15  
- Maintain manual override option during pilot  

## Action Items  
- Oriel to coordinate with telemetry team for data integration (due 2024-03-31)  
- Odalys to draft updated risk model parameters and testing plan (due 2024-04-10)  
- Nadezhda to oversee document portal enhancements with IT (due 2024-05-10)
